metadata.title: Claude, Equipped
metadata.subtitle: What a Cowork Plugin Actually Is
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: does a plugin just make Claude know more? Take the four components apart, name what they optimized for, and land the carry-out — a plugin doesn't add knowledge, it adds equipment (tools, reach, shortcuts) while the judgment stays yours.
metadata.anchor_pair: NB01 -> NB09 (the smart friend vs. the professional, paid off tuned to a real contract review)

beats.narration_text: Here's what people assume: install a plugin, Claude gets smarter — more facts, same generalist. That's not what's happening. A plugin doesn't add knowledge; it equips a specialist. So what does a plugin actually make Claude?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Does a plugin make Claude smarter?', hesitates on 'smarter', corrects to 'equipped', lands the real question

props.text:

make Claude
smarter?

beats.narration_text: Claude without plugins is a capable generalist — it can discuss any topic and apply broad knowledge to your situation. Optimized for breadth. Useful, but it's a smart friend helping with your taxes. They'll try. They're not an accountant.

shot.new_visual_element: A SMART FRIEND, NOT AN ACCOUNTANT

production_viz.label: A SMART FRIEND, NOT AN ACCOUNTANT
production_viz.caption: useful — but not a specialist

beats.narration_text: A plugin turns that generalist into the accountant — or the marketer, the sales researcher, the contract reviewer. Here's the trade: a mile of shallow knowledge for a well that goes deep in one domain. Breadth for depth, on purpose.

production_viz.label: ONE WELL, DUG DEEP
production_viz.caption: the accountant, the marketer, the reviewer

beats.narration_text: Tempting to think that's just a smarter prompt — more detail stuffed into the same conversation. Here's what's actually happening: a prompt can't log into your CRM, add a slash-command shortcut to your menu, or hand a multi-step job to a coordinating subagent. A plugin does all three. Different machinery, not more words.

production_viz.label: NOT JUST A SMARTER PROMPT
production_viz.caption: a prompt can't do any of the other three

beats.narration_text: Skills are the expertise piece — methodical frameworks, not generic tips. Here's what's actually happening: they switch on automatically when they're relevant. Ask a marketing question with marketing installed, and Claude reaches for the framework without being told to. They optimized for zero friction over explicit control.

Connectors are the reach. The sales plugin plugs into your CRM, the data plugin plugs into your spreadsheets. So Claude works on your actual business data — not hypothetical examples. That's the design choice: talk to your systems where they already live, don't ask you to copy-paste.

Commands are the shortcuts. Type slash-prospect-brief and the sales plugin researches a company. Slash-audit and marketing tears apart a page. Type slash inside Cowork to see the whole menu. One keystroke maps to one whole workflow — that's what they optimized for.

production_viz.label: ONE SLASH, ONE JOB
production_viz.caption: type slash to see them all

beats.narration_text: Subagents are the autonomy piece. Ask finance to build a model and it quietly coordinates the steps under the hood — gather, structure, run scenarios, compile — so you get one clean result instead of a pile of intermediate output. The trade is transparency for tidiness.

Here's the shift in one line: general knowledge becomes contextual capability. Legal reviews the actual contract you're about to sign. Marketing drafts in your brand voice, from your real style guide — not a hypothetical example. That's what changes when the four pieces sit on top of your own work.

Back to that friend and the accountant. Here's the difference in practice: asking a well-read friend what to watch for in a contract, versus asking someone who reviews contracts for a living. That gap is the whole reason a plugin is worth your time.

production_viz.label: THE FRIEND, AND THE PRO
production_viz.caption: that's the whole reason it's worth your time

beats.narration_text: Anthropic released these as open source. What that gets you: free — no charge beyond your paid plan. But open buys three more things — transparency instead of a black box, community fixes over time, and the ability to adjust a plugin that almost fits. Open source isn't a marketing word here; it's a design choice with four consequences.

production_viz.label: OPEN, SO IT BENDS
production_viz.caption: open source, beyond your paid plan

beats.narration_text: Out of the box, the sales plugin is useful. Configured with your process, your qualifying criteria, your positioning, it's dramatically more powerful. The real gain shows up after setup — customization is the next chapter. This works if you value your time enough to spend an hour tuning it; it fails if you expect magic on install.

production_viz.label: CONFIGURED HITS HARDER
production_viz.caption: the real gain shows up after setup

beats.narration_text: Four limits, stated plainly. Plugins don't hand Claude perfect judgment. They don't bypass its knowledge boundaries. They work only inside your existing access — your credentials, your permissions, nothing new. And they're tools, not replacements. That last one is the design decision, not the disclaimer.

Legal flags a scary clause; it can't weigh that clause against the deal you're doing. Finance builds the model; it can't tell you whether the assumptions fit your industry. Human judgment stays on the consequential calls. Here's what's happening: they optimized for equipping you, not for replacing you. That caveat isn't a disclaimer to skip — it's the instructions.

You don't need the whole catalog — most people run two or three. Start with your primary function, whatever you spend your day on. Add your biggest bottleneck, the thing you know you should do but don't. Then keep productivity running underneath as the foundation. Two or three is the sweet spot: enough to compound, not enough to lose the thread.

production_viz.label: TWO OR THREE
production_viz.caption: most people run two or three

beats.narration_text: A plugin doesn't make Claude know more — it makes Claude equipped: tools, reach, and shortcuts on your own work, with the judgment still yours.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: I run a small business and I'm new to Cowork plugins — walk me through choosing my first two. Ask what I spend my day on, name the function I keep neglecting, then tell me which plugin to install first, which to add second, and one way to customize each for my business. Go deeper: once you've picked those two, ask the same model what the third one costs you to skip — and whether it's worth the setup hour.
